items.ncert_ref: Many Ways to Multiply, 18 x 5 (chapter p.74)
items.question_text: What is 18 × 5? Five children found it in five ways. (1): Half of 18 is 9. 9 × 5 is 45 and 9 × 5 is 45. I added 45 and 45 together to get 90. (2): First, I doubled 18 to get 36. Then I doubled 36 to get 72 and then I added 18 to 72 to get 90. (3): I separated 18 into 8 and 10. 8 × 5 is 40. 10 × 5 is 50. Then I added 40 and 50 together to get 90. (4): 18 × 5 = 9 × 10. So, 90. (5): I did 20 × 5, which is 100. Then I took away 2 × 5, which is 10. So, 100 − 10 = 90. Do you think they are all correct? Why do you think so?
items.reason: The book picture is only the blue and green number boxes 18 and 5 and the children's sentences; every number is in the question text.
